text.p: Turkish chemical fertilizers and acid producer Bagfas Bandirma Gubre Fabrikalari A.S. targets total sales of $122 million in 1997, a senior company official said.
"We aim to increase our total turnover by 35.5 percent to $122 million this year, up from last year's $90 million," general manager Kemal Gencer told a news conference.
The turnover increase will rise in line with an expected 35.1 percent increase in fertilizer production to 600,000 tonnes this year from 444,000 tonnes in 1996.
Bagfas sold 551,000 tonnes of fertilizer last year.
Shares of the company opened at 30,000 lira on Tuesday and remained at the same level at the first session.

The company increased its phosphoric acid production -- the main raw material in fertilizer -- to 42,000 tonnes in 1996, up 31.2 percent from 32,000 tonnes in 1995. It targets to increase it to 100,000 tonnes this year.
The company's sulphuric acid production was unchanged last year at 317,000 tonnes.
Bagfas has a share of 14 percent in the five million tonne Turkish market. It produced 12 percent of the total output.
Bagfas will enter into export markets this year after an absence of one year in 1996 due to high domestic prices, Gencer said.
It reported 9.58 trillion lira turnover in 1996, against 5.83 trillion lira in 1995. Its net profit rose by 121.6 percent to 667 billion lira in 1996 from 300 billion lira in 1995.
Fertiliser consumption in Turkey, 80 tonnes per hectare, is still far below the European level of 210 tonnes, Gencer said.
